saml.description: SAML connector ignores offline_access and does not issue refresh tokens.
saml.note: Absence of refresh_token after SAML login is by design and should not be reported as a freshness failure.

saml.description: SAML connector does not support refresh tokens because SAML lacks a non-interactive requery mechanism.
saml.note: Session renewal expectations must be adjusted for SAML-backed identities.

saml.description: Dex uses SAML NameID as the unique user identifier and assumes it is stable and never changes.
saml.note: Differences between NameID and email/username attributes are expected; principal binding tests should key on NameID.

saml.description: Dex requires sending the initial AuthnRequest and validates InResponseTo; unsolicited SAML responses are not accepted.
saml.note: A rejected IdP-initiated or fabricated response without matching request context is expected behavior.

saml.constraint: Dex SAML login is SP-initiated only: the fuzzer MUST begin with start_oidc_auth and preserve the returned state/RelayState so saml_login posts a response matching Dex's AuthnRequest. Dex validates InResponseTo and will reject unsolicited or mismatched SAMLResponses.

For I1 signature-validation default tests, Dex documentation explicitly states insecureSkipSignatureValidation skips signature validation. To test insecure defaults, the SAML connector configuration MUST leave insecureSkipSignatureValidation unset/false; setting it true creates an intentional insecure configuration and is not a product vulnerability.

For I1 issuer-validation tests, ssoIssuer is OPTIONAL. If ssoIssuer is omitted, Dex may not enforce issuer matching against a configured expected issuer. A valid saml_issuer_mismatch test MUST configure ssoIssuer to the trusted IdP entity ID; otherwise acceptance of a wrong Issuer is ambiguous because issuer checking was never configured.

For I5 audience-binding tests, Dex uses entityIssuer as the expected AudienceRestriction value when set; otherwise it uses redirectURI. The fuzzer MUST compute the expected audience from entityIssuer if configured, else redirectURI. Testing with the wrong expected audience will misclassify results.

For I1/I5 destination and audience tests, redirectURI matching is exact. If the SAML assertion/response contains a Destination element, it must exactly equal redirectURI. Do not treat redirectURI as pattern-matched or prefix-matched.

For I4 principal-binding tests, Dex uses the SAML NameID as the user's unique identifier and assumes it is unique and immutable. usernameAttr/emailAttr do not define the principal key. Therefore saml_email_binding_collision should expect binding by NameID, not by email; changing email alone should not switch the downstream principal.

For I4 multi-identity scenarios, NameID format is controlled by nameIDPolicyFormat and defaults to persistent if unset. The fuzzer SHOULD keep NameID values stable and unique across logins and should not assume email-style identifiers unless nameIDPolicyFormat is explicitly configured accordingly.

For I5 group-based authorization tests, allowedGroups is exact list-membership only; documentation describes a whitelist of SAML groups, not glob or regex matching. For multi-identity tests requiring different group values to pass the same connector, the fuzzer MUST omit allowedGroups entirely rather than set wildcard values like '*', which would be treated as a literal group name.

For I5 group filtering tests, filterGroups=true does not deny authentication by itself; it removes groups not in allowedGroups from the emitted claims. Authentication gating is based on membership checks against configured allowedGroups when groupsAttr is set and groups scope is requested. Distinguish claim filtering from login denial when interpreting results.

For I4 group type-confusion tests, groupsDelim changes parsing semantics: without groupsDelim, multiple groups are expected as repeated attributes; with groupsDelim, a single string attribute is split by the delimiter. The fuzzer MUST control this setting to avoid false positives when comparing string vs list group representations.
Dex SAML connector ignores offline_access and does not support refresh tokens by design. Do not flag absence of refresh_token in token responses after SAML login as an I2 freshness bug.

For I2 replay tests, Dex documentation states it persists state to prevent replays. SAML replay tests should reuse the same assertion ID (fixed_assertion_id) across two saml_login submissions in the same configured deployment. A control login with a fresh assertion ID should also be included to distinguish replay rejection from generic SAML misconfiguration.

For I2 freshness tests involving code exchange, auth code lifetime is controlled by expiry.authRequests in configuration. The docs specify duration strings only and do not define a 0 or negative sentinel. The fuzzer MUST NOT assume 0 disables or means immediate expiry; if testing code expiry, use explicit nonzero durations in config and a control exchange within the valid window.

Dex SAML login is SP-initiated only. The fuzzer MUST start the flow with GET /auth and preserve the returned state/relay context before posting SAMLResponse to /callback/{connector_id}; posting an unsolicited SAMLResponse without a matching AuthnRequest/InResponseTo will be rejected by design.

For I1 signature-validation default tests, Dex documentation explicitly allows disabling signature validation with insecureSkipSignatureValidation=true and warns it is only for testing. A valid insecure-default test MUST distinguish omitted config from explicitly disabled validation; acceptance when insecureSkipSignatureValidation is enabled is by design, not a bug.

For I1 issuer-validation tests, ssoIssuer is optional. If ssoIssuer is not configured, Dex may not enforce expected issuer matching against a configured IdP issuer value. To test issuer enforcement, the fuzzer MUST configure ssoIssuer and then send a mismatched assertion Issuer; otherwise a successful login may reflect missing configuration rather than a validation bypass.

For I5 audience-binding tests, Dex uses redirectURI as the expected SAML audience unless entityIssuer is specified, in which case entityIssuer overrides redirectURI as the required audience. The fuzzer MUST compute the expected AudienceRestriction target from entityIssuer when present, otherwise from redirectURI; using the wrong expected audience will misclassify results.

For I1 destination-binding tests, if the SAML response/assertion status contains a Destination element, Dex requires it to match redirectURI exactly. The fuzzer MUST use the exact configured callback URL when crafting Destination or a rejection is expected and not evidence of another invariant failure.

Dex binds the downstream unique user identity to the SAML NameID value. For I4 collision tests, changing email/username attributes without changing NameID should not be expected to create a different principal. To test principal-binding failures, vary NameID itself; emailAttr and usernameAttr only affect mapped claims, not the unique identifier.

For I4 multi-identity scenarios, nameIDPolicyFormat is not a wildcard or pattern-matching control; it only requests the NameID format from the IdP and defaults to persistent. The fuzzer MUST NOT treat it as a subject constraint. Distinct NameID byte strings are the relevant identity inputs for collision and normalization tests.

For I5 group-based authorization tests, allowedGroups is exact list-membership filtering, not glob or regex matching. filterGroups only controls whether non-allowed groups are excluded from claims; it does not change allowedGroups matching semantics. For multi-group scenarios, the fuzzer MUST supply exact group names and MUST NOT use '*' expecting wildcard behavior.

For I5 group filtering interpretation, when groupsAttr is set and allowedGroups is configured, Dex checks membership in configured allowedGroups for authentication. If filterGroups=true, groups not in allowedGroups are removed from emitted claims. Therefore a login failure for a user outside allowedGroups is by design, and a reduced groups claim set under filterGroups=true is also by design.
Dex SAML connector does not support refresh tokens and ignores offline_access. The fuzzer MUST NOT treat absence of refresh_token or inability to refresh a SAML-derived session as an I2/I3 bug.

For I2 control-vs-attack interpretation on SAML freshness tests, include a control SAML login with valid Conditions and expected audience alongside attack variants such as remove_conditions=true or wrong audience. Without a successful control, a failed attack login cannot be distinguished from broken connector/client setup.

Dex SAML login is SP-initiated only: the fuzzer MUST start the flow first and preserve the returned request state so the posted SAMLResponse matches Dex's expected InResponseTo. Unprompted SAML responses are rejected by design because Dex sends the initial AuthnRequest and validates InResponseTo.

For I5 audience-binding tests, Dex uses redirectURI as the expected SAML AudienceRestriction unless entityIssuer is specified; when entityIssuer is set, it overrides redirectURI as the required audience. The fuzzer MUST compute the expected audience from entityIssuer if present, otherwise from redirectURI, or wrong-audience/no-audience tests will be misinterpreted.

For I1/I5 destination and audience tests, if the SAML assertion/response contains a Destination element it must match redirectURI exactly. Failures caused by Destination mismatch are setup errors, not evidence about signature or audience validation. Keep Destination correct unless the test specifically targets Destination handling.

Dex SAML connector uses NameID as the user's unique identifier and assumes it is unique and never changes. For I4 principal-binding tests, vary NameID to test identity separation/collision; changing only email or username attributes may not change the bound principal. In particular, saml_email_binding_collision should not be expected against Dex's documented default because binding is by NameID, not email.

nameIDPolicyFormat defaults to persistent if unspecified. For I4 tests involving mutable identifiers such as email-style NameIDs, the fuzzer MUST explicitly configure a non-persistent format if the scenario depends on that upstream behavior; otherwise Dex will request persistent NameID semantics by default.

allowedGroups is list-membership filtering, not wildcard/regex matching, and filterGroups only controls whether non-allowed groups are excluded from claims. For multi-identity I4 scenarios requiring different group values to pass the same connector, the fuzzer MUST OMIT allowedGroups entirely rather than set wildcard-like values. A literal '*' would only match a group literally named '*'.

For I5 group-authorization tests, when groupsAttr is set and allowedGroups is configured, authentication succeeds only if the user is a member of at least one configured allowed group; with filterGroups=true, groups outside allowedGroups are removed from emitted claims. The fuzzer MUST account for both admission filtering and claim filtering when interpreting missing or reduced groups.

SAML connector does not support refresh tokens and ignores offline_access. Tests that expect refresh_token issuance, refresh-based replay, or offline session behavior are invalid for Dex SAML and MUST NOT be treated as failures.

For I2 freshness tests on the downstream Dex token flow, include a control login using a valid authorization flow alongside any attack case. A failed code exchange or callback may result from broken flow state or connector setup rather than token freshness, especially because SAML login is interactive and stateful.

Dex token exchange is documented only for OIDC connectors, not SAML. The fuzzer MUST NOT attempt RFC 8693 token_exchange tests in the SAML profile; absence or rejection is by design and not an authorization-binding bug.
